name: Hot Cross Buns with Candied Citrus & Raisins

instructions.primary_message: FOR THE BUNS: Place yeast and warm water (105° F - 115° F) in a large mixing bowl; whisk to combine and set aside to hydrate, about 5 minutes. (Alternatively, you can place them in the bowl of a stand mixer.)

Meanwhile, cut butter into small pieces and place in a small saucepan along with the milk. Set the pan over medium-low and heat, stirring often, until butter is just melted and milk is lightly warm to the touch (105°F - 115°F). Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
5 tbsp butter, unsalted
1 cup whole milk

instructions.primary_message: Add the warm milk mixture, egg, sugar, and spices to the bowl with the hydrated yeast; whisk to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 egg
3 tbsp granulated sugar
1 tsp salt
½ tsp cinnamon, ground
¼ tsp cloves, ground

instructions.primary_message: Gradually add bread flour to the bowl, mixing by hand, until combined. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer with dough hook attachment, mix on low speed until combined, about 1 minute.)

Gradually add 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour to the bowl, mixing by hand, until combined. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer with dough hook attachment, mix on low speed until combined, 1 minute more.)
Add additional all-purpose flour to the bowl, a few tablespoons at a time, to create a dough that is moist but not sticky to the touch. (You may not need the full ½-cup of additional flour.)

Cut candied orange and lemon peel into small pieces. Sprinkle over the dough, along with the raisins, then knead by hand until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer, add peel and raisins to the bowl, then knead on medium-low speed until dough is smooth and elastic, 5-8 minutes.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp candied orange peel
2 tbsp candied lemon peel
⅓ cup raisins

instructions.primary_message: Coat a clean large bowl with a thin layer of oil. Place dough in the bowl, turn to coat in the oil, then loosely cover bowl with plastic wrap. Set the bowl in a warm place (70°F – 80°F), until dough has doubled in volume, about 2 hours.
Once the dough has doubled, remove the plastic wrap (reserving it for later use), and press the dough down with your hands to release the air.
Coat a large (9 x 13-inch) baking dish with a thin layer of butter.

Divide the dough into 12 equal-sized pieces. On an unfloured surface, roll each piece of dough into a ball. Place the dough balls in the prepared baking dish, arranging them in three rows of four, with equal space in between. Loosely cover the buns with the reserved plastic wrap. Set the baking dish in a warm place (70°F – 80°F), until buns have doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
About 15 minutes before the buns are ready, preheat the oven to 425°F.

FOR THE TOPPING: While the oven is heating, place flour and water in a small bowl, then stir until a thick, smooth paste forms (you may need to use an additional 1-2 tsp water to get the right consistency). Transfer the paste to a small resealable plastic bag.

Once the buns have doubled in volume, remove the plastic wrap and discard. Cut a small hole in one corner of the plastic bag. Holding onto it like a piping bag, pipe two perpendicular lines over the surface of each bun to create a cross.
Place buns in the oven and bake, undisturbed, until golden brown, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm honey in a small saucepan set over medium-low heat. Cover and set aside.
When the buns are done, remove from the oven. Brush with warm honey and set aside to cool.
Once the buns are cool, remove from the baking dish and tear apart.
